components.source_check: Durrett v5 p.84 (a series converges when lim_N of its partial sums exists) and p.85 (w_M = sup_{m,n>=M}|S_m-S_n|): both present, with the finite real limit, almost-sure, absolute and conditional convergence, centering and finite-subfamily independence made explicit.

Durrett p.85 (w_M decreasing to 0 gives a Cauchy sequence). Countable Cauchy description, measurability of w_M, tail membership, X_n -> 0, finite-change invariance of convergence and absolute convergence, and the 0-1 law are each proved in written steps.

Durrett Thm 2.5.5 and its Remark (p.84): same hypotheses (independent, mean zero, finite variances), same first-crossing decomposition with the cross term killed by independence; the Chebyshev remark is preserved as the statement that a bound for S_n alone does not give the maximal assertion. Dependent and uncentered failures are worked.
Durrett Thm 2.5.6 (pp.84-85): hypotheses and the maximal-inequality / w_M proof are preserved; the added L2 identities are proved (Fatou, Cauchy-Schwarz).
Handbook elementary converse used for the direct necessity proof; fourth-moment identity, the Paley-Zygmund-type bound and the bounded converse are proved in full.
Product-space copy, finite-subfamily independence, centering, symmetry by the coordinate swap, the 2A bound, Var(Z_n)=2Var(Y_n) and the convergence transfer are all proved.
Both directions proved; conditional convergence of the mean series allowed and exhibited in C013 item 1.
Durrett Thm 2.5.8 (p.85): Y_i = X_i 1(|X_i| <= A), deletion truncation with endpoints retained; the three series as in the source.

Durrett Thm 2.5.8 (p.85): statement for any A > 0, the source sufficiency proof (2.5.6 plus Borel-Cantelli) preserved, necessity proved without the CLT; one-cutoff/every-cutoff equivalence and the probability-zero failure proved.

Durrett Thm 3.4.10 (p.148): rows 1<=m<=n independent, mean zero, conditions (i)-(ii), conclusion in CDF form (equivalent since Phi is continuous); its full proof is on the route at thm:p15-clt-lindeberg-feller.

Durrett Example 3.4.12 (pp.150-151): necessity of (i), the c_n rows, Lindeberg sum zero once 2A/c_n^{1/2} < eps, T_n => 0, the non-random S_n - T_n contradiction (the Exercise 3.2.13 step written out), and (ii) by differences; initial zero c_n handled.
Durrett Example 2.5.7 (p.85): alpha > 1/2 sufficiency via 2.5.6, necessity via 2.5.8, absolute convergence iff alpha > 1; all real alpha classified with the p-series criterion proved.
Handbook boundary examples (conditional mean series, each condition failing alone, unbounded summands with divergent variances, dependence and centering failures), each computed.
Durrett pp.85-87 (Kronecker 2.5.9, SLLN 2.5.10 by random series): every pointer of the boundary resolves on the route to complete entries; the boundary claims are accurate.
